A new chapter of meaning. It is created because what the artifact means changed, not merely because its JSON shape or generated documentation changed.
A byte change alone does not prove semantic change.
A claim that meaning is preserved is reviewable evidence, not automatic equivalence.
A semantic successor requires explicit owner selection and applicable lineage.
NewSemanticEpoch(a_before,a_after) iff MaterialNormativeMeaning(a_before) != MaterialNormativeMeaning(a_after). RepresentationChanged and MeaningEqual does not imply NewSemanticEpoch.

A Semantic Epoch is one immutable owner-selected version of an artifact's normative meaning. A successor Semantic Epoch is required exactly when the owner determines that the artifact's identity-preserving normative meaning, scope, exclusions, owned model, or semantic contracts materially changed. Representation-only revisions and derived refreshes do not create Semantic Epochs.

unresolved_notes: C28 admits the exact positive Definition without accepting this formal translation or selecting any existing successor.
Selected epoch and assessment universes are candidate scopes; complete canonical artifact/epoch/change universes need owner maps.
Exact typed identities and reference selectors are nominations rather than authenticated semantic identity or selected content.
Epoch immutability and owner-selected posture are declarations, not storage enforcement or executed owner selection.
One nominated owner selection per epoch and one successor per assessment do not settle aggregation, uniqueness or alias universes.
Identity-preserving successor assessments use equal artifact identity references; identity-changing cases need explicit source correspondence.
MaterialNormativeMeaning is represented by a separate aggregate meaning reference alongside five semantic coordinates, not equated only to raw normative prose.
The short material-meaning iff and richer owner determination criterion are composed as necessary declaration coherence; source precedence remains owner pending.
Material judgement is the inclusive OR of five assessed dimensions, without forcing every reference difference to be material.
A material dimension nominates unequal coordinate references; actual difference and materiality are independent source/content judgements.
Representation difference is independent of material meaning and includes abstract schema/encoding/projection correspondence still pending.
Byte-change declarations are neither sufficient nor necessary axioms for a successor; actual byte/content maps remain unaccepted.
Representation-only,schema-only,encoding-only and derived-refresh classifications retain equal declared aggregate meaning and no new epoch.
Before-epoch and before-artifact correspondence identifies an explicit predecessor but does not authenticate its history.
New epoch references differ from predecessors and bind after artifacts; global epoch identity injectivity is not inferred.
Successor owner selection,predecessor,material delta and lineage references are exact records, not executed decisions or lineage creation.
Material delta before/after selectors match aggregate meanings while real semantic delta fidelity remains independent.
Lineage recorded/applicable posture cannot prove actual applicable lineage or authorize creation.
A preservation claim carries reviewable evidence; the claim does not force meaning equality and can coexist with a contested material-change assessment.
Unused successor and evidence selectors remain total without asserting optional record existence or obligations.
Source scope,claim ceiling,examples and notation are accounted without turning filesystem labels or reconstruction metadata into succession.
Finite T/I witnesses and exact source string accounting do not accept shared meanings,source fidelity,whole translation or whole proof.
